name: Satellite Imagery
title: Satellite Imagery
answer: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers optical, radar, thermal and hyperspectral pictures of the Earth's surface, often collected by public and commercial constellations. Analysts use it to measure physical activity that shows up in economic statistics with a lag, such as parking lot occupancy, oil storage levels, ship traffic, crop health, construction progress and mining output. The data is not just the image, it includes derived counts, areas, changes and time series. It sits alongside other alternative data in research on supply chains, commodities and industrial activity.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers optical, radar, thermal and hyperspectral pictures of the Earth's surface, often collected by public and commercial constellations. Analysts use it to measure physical activity that shows up in economic statistics with a lag, such as parking lot occupancy, oil storage levels, ship traffic, crop health, construction progress and mining output. The data is not just the image, it includes derived counts, areas, changes and time series. It sits alongside other alternative data in research on supply chains, commodities and industrial activity.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on satellite constellations, ground stations and cloud computing. Public programs like Landsat and Sentinel provide free imagery, while commercial providers sell higher resolution or more frequent captures. Processing happens in object storage and GPU clusters, with geospatial databases and image tiling services. Downstream users often access results through APIs or dashboards rather than raw scenes.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical pipeline starts with tasking or selecting scenes, then applies orthorectification, atmospheric correction and cloud masking. Analysts tile the images and train computer vision models for object detection, semantic segmentation and change detection. Time series methods track the same location across many dates to separate real change from noise. Validation uses ground truth, higher resolution reference data or known events, and the output is often a numeric index rather than a picture.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk around satellite imagery include licensing terms, national security restrictions, privacy rules and export controls. Resolution limits and revisit restrictions vary by country, and commercial providers often prohibit resale or certain uses. Provenance matters because a derived signal can be wrong if the scene is cloudy, the model is biased or the location is misregistered. The site's 215 compliance and regulation pages show how many rules can touch this data, from imagery licensing to data protection.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more satellites, higher revisit rates and cheaper access to imagery. AI models are making it easier to turn raw scenes into real time indicators for methane leaks, deforestation, construction and shipping. Fusion with other alternative data, such as vessel tracking or weather, is likely to grow. At the same time, crowding, regulation and the need for transparent validation will shape what can be used in practice.
